parole.significato: Forms names of hearing impairments.

parole.significato: flower

parole.significato: Having flowers with a specific behavior or appearance.

parole.significato: One who transforms into (usually an animal).

parole.significato: humanity; mankind
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἄνθρωπος (ánthrōpos, “human”).

parole.significato: forms medical terms for the onset of certain changes in puberty

parole.significato: Forms names of speech impairments, especially relating to the ordering of words.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἄρθρον (árthron, “joint, articulation”) + -ia.

parole.significato: Contest
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ancient Greek ἆθλον (âthlon, “contest”).

parole.significato: Used to form adjectives describing a method of living.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek βιωτικός (biōtikós, “of life”), from βίος (bíos, “life”).

parole.significato: an immature cell or tissue
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ancient Greek βλᾰστός (blăstós, “germ, sprout”).

parole.significato: Forming nouns relating to a bending or curvature.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek κάμψις (kámpsis).

parole.significato: Forms nouns relating to a heart condition.

parole.significato: Part of a fruit or fruiting body.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek καρπός (karpós, “fruit, grain”).

parole.significato: Having a specified number or type of fruit or fruiting bodies or part thereof.

parole.significato: A tumour.

parole.significato: Related to the geologic era called the Cenozoic, the current one.
parole.testo: From Cenozoic. From Ancient Greek καινός (kainós, “new”).

parole.significato: Puncture and aspiration of
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek κέντησις (kéntēsis, “the act of pricking”), from κεντέω (kentéō, “I prick”).

parole.significato: Having a specified number of centres.
parole.testo: Representing a combining form of Ancient Greek κεντρικός (kentrikós, “central”). Cognate with Bengali -কেন্দ্রিক (-kendrik)

parole.significato: head
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek κεφαλή (kephalḗ).

parole.significato: defecation
parole.testo: Representing the Ancient Greek χέζω (khézō, “I defecate”) + -ῐ́ᾱ (-ĭ́ā, “-ia”, suffix forming abstract nouns).

parole.significato: An organism, especially a plant or plant pathogen, that spreads by a specified agent, or in a specified manner.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek χωρέω (khōréō, “I move, spread”).

parole.significato: A group of habitats with a similar environment and a similar biota.
parole.testo: Backformation from biochore, from bio-+Ancient Greek χώρα (khṓra, “country”).

parole.significato: Used to form the names of 4-dimensional solids bounded by a certain number of cells/polyhedra (polychora).
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek χῶρον (khôron, “room”).

parole.significato: Producing or changing color in a certain way.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek χρώς (khrṓs, “color, complexion”) + -ic.

parole.significato: Relating to time.
parole.testo: Ultimately from Ancient Greek χρόνος (khrónos) + -ous.

parole.significato: fracture (having a fracture of such a form)
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek κλᾰ́σῐς (klắsĭs, “breaking, fracture”) (via French -clase), from κλάω (kláō, “I break”).

parole.significato: Fragmentation, breaking
parole.testo: Ultimately from Ancient Greek κλᾰστός (klăstós, “broken”). Doublet of -clase.

parole.significato: Something that breaks or destroys.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek κλαστός (klastós, “broken”), verbal adjective of κλάω (kláō, “to break”).

parole.significato: Closure, blockage, shutting.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek κλεῖσις (kleîsis).

parole.significato: having a specified slope
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek κλίνω (klínō, “to lean”). Cognate with Latin clīnō.

parole.significato: hollowed out, relating to concavity
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek κοῖλος (koîlos, “hollow”).

parole.significato: Combines with the prefixes for 1–9 to form complex prefixes referring to 21–29.
parole.testo: From icosa-, itself from words like icosagon and icosahedron, which ultimately derive from Ancient Greek εἴκοσι (eíkosi).

parole.significato: rule (in the sense of governing).
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek -κρατία (-kratía), from κράτος (krátos, “power”).

parole.significato: temperament, constituent pattern.
parole.testo: Ultimately from Ancient Greek κρᾶσις (krâsis, “mixing, tempering”), often via Latin -crāsia and, additionally, Old French -crasie.

parole.significato: A participant in a specified form of government.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek κράτος (krátos, “power, might”), modelled after words of Ancient Greek origin such as democrat and aristocrat. From Proto-Indo-European *kret- (English hard).

parole.significato: Used to form names of acridine derivatives.
parole.testo: Contraction of acridine. Ancient Greek κρίνω (krínō, “to separate”).

parole.significato: Cryptography.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek κρυπτός (kruptós, literally “hidden, concealed, private, secret”).

parole.significato: skin or covering
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek δέρμα (dérma, “skin”).

parole.significato: skin or skin disease
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek δέρμα (dérma, “skin”).

parole.significato: having a specified type skin
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek δέρμα (dérma, “skin”), genitive δέρματος (dérmatos) + -ous.

parole.significato: Binding, fusion.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ancient Greek δέσῐς (désĭs, “binding together”), from δέω (déō, “to bind, tie, fasten”) + -σῐς (-sĭs, nominal suffix).

parole.significato: thirst
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek δῐ́ψᾰ (dĭ́psă, “thirst”).

parole.significato: Forms placenames related to racetracks (now especially large covered racetracks) or similar structures.
parole.testo: Derived from Ancient Greek δρόμος (drómos, “running; racetrack”).

parole.significato: Running or moving in a specified manner.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek δρόμος (drómos, “race, running”) + -ic.

parole.significato: running or moving in a specified manner
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek δρόμος (drómos, “race, running”) + -ous.

parole.significato: The quality or state of running or moving in a specified manner.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek δρόμος (drómos, “race, running”) + -y.

parole.significato: Forms names of certain types of motors and electrical circuits.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek δύναμις (dúnamis, “force”), compare -dynamic. Originally prevalent in now often genericized trademarks.

parole.significato: The surgical removal of.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἐκτομή (ektomḗ, “a cutting out of”), from ἐκτέμνω (ektémnō, “to cut out”), from ἐκ (ek, “out”) + τέμνω (témnō, “to cut”).

parole.significato: Indicating a fundamental unit in some kind of structure, chiefly linguistic structure.
parole.testo: Extracted from phoneme, from Ancient Greek φώνημα (phṓnēma, “sound”), from φωνέω (phōnéō, “to sound”), from φωνή (phōnḗ, “sound”).

parole.significato: cellular tissue
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ancient Greek ἔγχυμα (énkhuma, “infusion”).

parole.significato: work
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek -εργία (-ergía), from ἔργον (érgon, “work”).

parole.significato: Used to form adjectives, meaning "pertaining to", derived from nouns, most of which end in -esis and -esy.
parole.testo: Ultimately from Ancient Greek -ητικός (-ētikós).

parole.significato: Forms the names of functional diseases or of conditions such as pyrexia or cachexia.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἕξις (héxis, “possession, condition”), from ἔχω (ékhō, “to have”).

parole.significato: Having the specified number or form of marriage.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek γάμος (gámos, “union, marriage”), equivalent to -gamy + -ous.

parole.significato: Used to form nouns describing forms of marriage.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek -γαμία (-gamía), from γάμος (gámos, “marriage”).

parole.significato: Of or relating to the stomach.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek γαστήρ (gastḗr, “stomach”). Compare the prefix gastro-.

parole.significato: production
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ancient Greek -γένεια (-géneia).

parole.significato: Used to form nouns relating to the tongue.
parole.testo: From the Ancient Greek γλῶσσα (glôssa, “tongue”). Compare gloss-, glott-.

parole.significato: language
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek γλῶσσᾰ (glôssă, “tongue; language”).

parole.significato: Forming nouns relating to the jaws or mouthparts.
parole.testo: Ultimately from Ancient Greek γνάθος (gnáthos, “jaw”), frequently after formations in New Latin -gnatha, -gnathi, or French -gnathe.

parole.significato: Scientific knowledge of a subject.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek -γνωσία (-gnōsía), from γνῶσις (gnôsis). Doublet of gnosis.

parole.significato: Forms the names of plane figures containing a given number of internal angles, and thus bounded by that number of line…
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek γωνία (gōnía, “corner, angle”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵónu (“knee”).

parole.significato: Productive, fertile, fruitful
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek γόνιμος (gónimos, “productive, fertile, fruitful”).

parole.significato: A reproductive structure of some organisms
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek γονή (gonḗ, “engendering”) + -ium (“structure”).

parole.significato: Forms nouns that describe the genesis of a class of thing.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek γονή (gonḗ, “generation”).

parole.significato: Something written, drawn or otherwise recorded.
parole.testo: From γράμμα (grámma, “written character, letter, that which is drawn”), from γράφω (gráphō, “to scratch, to scrape, to graze”).

parole.significato: that writes
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek -γράφος (-gráphos, “that writes, describes”), from γράφω (gráphō, “to scratch, to scrape, to graze”), whence also -graphy.

parole.significato: someone who writes about a specified subject, or in a specified manner
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek γράφω (gráphō, “I draw, write or describe”) + -er.

parole.significato: Forms names of writing impairments.
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek -γρᾰφῐ́ᾱ (-grăphĭ́ā, “writing, drawing”).

parole.significato: Forming adjectives pertaining to writing (of a type specified by the first element).
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek -γραφικός (-graphikós), or formed in English from -graphy + -ic.

parole.significato: the state of having a specific number of wives
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek γυνή (gunḗ, “woman, female”).

parole.significato: Forms adjectives referring to solid figures bounded by a certain number of planes (polyhedra).
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ancient Greek ἕδρα (hédra, “face of a geometrical solid”) + -al.

parole.significato: Forms the names of solid figures bounded by a certain number of planes (polyhedra).
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἕδρα (hédra, “face of a geometrical solid”).

parole.significato: Relating to the hyoid bone.

parole.significato: Of or relating to a physician.

parole.significato: Forms a noun meaning a specialty medical field of practice.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἰατρός (iatrós, “doctor”) + -ics.

parole.significato: Forms names of specialized fields of medical practice.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἰατρεία (iatreía, “healing, medical treatment”), from ἰατρός (iatrós, “doctor”).

parole.significato: Forms names of types of trace fossils.

parole.significato: Used to form diminutive nouns.

parole.significato: Forms names of body parts, mainly of invertebrate animals, fungi and plants.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek -ίδιον (-ídion, “diminutive”).

parole.significato: An anthropometric reference point.
parole.testo: Possibly reanalysed from inion, which is of Ancient Greek origin. In many cases also analysable as the neuter form of an Ancient Greek adjective in -ιος (-ios).

parole.significato: Together with apo- and peri-, forms names of specific apoapsides and periapsides.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἀπόγειον (apógeion, “apogee”), containing -ιον (-ion). Compare also -ium.

parole.significato: Of or relating to an island or peninsula in Greece or the Hellenic sphere.
parole.testo: Back-formation of Cypriot, from Ancient Greek Κυπριώτης (Kupriṓtēs, “Cypriot”).

parole.significato: Used to form nouns of action, process, or result based on the accompanying verb ending in -ise or -ize.

Doublet of -ismus. Many English nouns in -ism are loans of Greek nouns in -ισμός (-ismós), often via Latin and Fre

parole.significato: Used to form nouns denoting condition, action, or process.
parole.testo: Ultimately from Ancient Greek -σις (-sis).

parole.significato: And, used in forming words using Greek numeral prefixes.

parole.significato: Forms names of specific cytokines.

parole.significato: movement, motion
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ancient Greek κίνησις (kínēsis, “motion, movement”), from κινέω (kinéō, “I move, put in motion”).

parole.significato: A flagellate of a given type.

parole.significato: sexual predilection; paraphilia
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek λαγνεία (lagneía, “sexual intercourse; lasciviousness”).

parole.significato: sexual predilection; paraphilia
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek λαγνεία (lagneía, “sexual intercourse; lasciviousness”).

parole.significato: Forming nouns denoting abnormal or disordered forms of speech.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek λαλιά (laliá, “talk, chat”).

parole.significato: A (language) variety.

parole.significato: a specified form of possession (noun sense 5 or noun sense 6), fit or seizure
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek λῆψις (lêpsis, “seizure”) and epilepsy, which is from Ancient Greek ἐπιληψίᾱ (epilēpsíā).

parole.significato: Of or relating to a condition of seizing, as in nympholeptic.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek λῆψις (lêpsis, “taking hold, seizing”) + -ic, as in Ancient Greek ληπτικός (lēptikós).

parole.significato: A part of a stratified lake.

parole.significato: Used to form the names of rocks and minerals.

parole.significato: Forms names of speech disorders.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek -λογία (-logía, “speech”).

parole.significato: decomposition or breakdown
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek λύσις (lúsis, “a loosening”). Compare lysis.

parole.significato: Word-forming element used in making nouns corresponding to nouns in -lysis and adjectives in -lytic.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ancient Greek λυτός (lutós, “loosed”), verbal adjective of λύειν (lúein, “to unfasten, loose, loosen, untie”).

parole.significato: Forming nouns with the sense of ‘battle, fight’.
parole.testo: Representing Ancient Greek -μαχία (-makhía), from μάχη (mákhē, “battle, fight; dispute”).

parole.significato: An abnormality of the breast.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek μαστός (mastós, “breast”).

parole.significato: Suffix denoting a strong hatred and opposition of whatever thing the suffix is attached to.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ancient Greek μάστῐξ (mástĭx, “whip, scourge, plague”).

parole.significato: enlargement
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek μεγάλος (megálos), further μέγας (mégas).

parole.significato: Used to form words relating to chemical structure, denoting parts of a molecule, for example, monomer (one part), dimer…
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek μέρος (méros, “part”).

parole.significato: Forming nouns with the sense of part, segment
parole.testo: Derived from Ancient Greek μέρος (méros, “part”).

parole.significato: Refers to the manner in which a body of water stratifies.

parole.significato: Hating (something); averse to (something).

parole.significato: shape, form, structure
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ancient Greek μορφή (morphḗ, “form, shape”).

parole.significato: having a specific shape or form
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek μορφή (morphḗ, “form, shape”) + -ic, equivalent to -morph + -ic.

parole.significato: Shaped or formed.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek μορφή (morphḗ, “shape”), partly after -μορφία (-morphía).

parole.significato: Used to form words used for categorising fungi based on their evolutionary origin, life history, growth form, or ecolog…
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek μύκης (múkēs, “mushroom, fungus, mushroom-shaped objects”).

parole.significato: Used to form names of antibiotics that pertain to fungi
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek μύκης (múkēs, “fungus”).

parole.significato: Pressed, closed.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ναστός (nastós, “pressed”), from the verb νάσσω (nássō).

parole.significato: relating to a nastic change
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ναστός (nastós, “pressed”), from the verb νάσσω (nássō). By surface analysis, -nast + -y.

parole.significato: Forms nouns meaning voyager or traveller
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ναύτης (naútēs, “sailor”).

parole.significato: Characteristic of, pertaining to, or possessing a filiform structure.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek νῆμᾰ (nêmă, “thread”). Compare nemat-.

parole.significato: Denotes an expression with a specified number of terms.
parole.testo: Derived from Ancient Greek νομός (nomós, “portion, part”), compare binomial.

parole.significato: Used to form nouns, referring to a book of knowledge on the specified topic.
parole.testo: Most likely from the name of the fictional Necronomicon, or from Ancient Greek νομῐκόν (nomĭkón), the neuter form of νομικός (nomikós, “relating to laws”) (also used in the titles of various real works, like the Nomicon of Photius, or the 18th century Nomicon Procheiron of Michael Photinopoulos).

parole.significato: The rules of a discipline.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek νόμος (nómos, “law”). The addition of an English prefix thus indicates the "laws" of the discipline or area denoted by the prefix. By surface analysis, -nomy + -ics.

parole.significato: Way, path, travel.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ancient Greek ὁδός (hodós, “road, path, way, journey, travel, means, method, system”).

parole.significato: Characterized by.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek -ώδης (-ṓdēs, “form, likeness”).

parole.significato: tooth; toothed
parole.testo: From the oblique stem of Ancient Greek ὀδούς (odoús).

parole.significato: branch of dentistry
parole.testo: Formed from the suffixation of ὀδόντ- (odónt-), the stem of the Ancient Greek ὀδούς (odoús, “tooth”), with the English suffix -ia; compare the Latin -odontia and the French -odontie.

parole.significato: pain
parole.testo: From international scientific vocabulary, reflecting a New Latin combining form, from Ancient Greek ὀδύνη (odúnē, “sorrow, grief, anguish, unhappiness”).

parole.significato: Forming nouns indicating disease or morbidity.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek -ωμα (-ōma), from verbs in -όω (-óō) + -μα (-ma) (from Proto-Indo-European *-mn̥), which lengthens a preceding vowel.

parole.significato: A mass of something.
parole.testo: Alteration of -oma, from Ancient Greek -ωμα (-ōma). Only partially cognate to -some (“body”), from σῶμα (sôma, “body”), in that both share the case ending -μα (-ma), but the ω is unrelated.

parole.significato: Forms nouns meaning “a study of the totality of something”.
parole.testo: From -ome (“whole of class”) + -ics, both via international scientific vocabulary and New Latin ultimately from Ancient Greek.

parole.significato: Used to form names of conditions involving a tumor, swelling, or mass.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ὄγκος (ónkos, “tumor”).

parole.significato: Indicating a life-form or life-stage, especially with regards to reproduction.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek -ων (-ōn), the present participle ending ("-ing"). Scientific usage possibly originates from -biont.

parole.significato: Used to form nouns describing the study, formation, or use of words or names.
parole.testo: From international scientific vocabulary, reflecting a New Latin combining form (-onymia), from Ancient Greek ὄνομα (ónoma, “name”)/Ancient Greek ὄνυμα (ónuma, “name”) (whence also onoma) + -ia; compare also ὄνομα § Derived terms.

parole.significato: Eye
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ὠπός (ōpós), genitive of ὤψ (ṓps, “eye”).

parole.significato: Forming compound nouns denoting specific deficiencies of sight.
