parole.testo: From Ancient Greek, from ὕστερον (hústeron, “latter, arriving late”) + πρότερον (próteron, “former, before”).

parole.significato: The science of remedies, or of therapeutics.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἴαματο- (íamato-), stem of ἴαμα (íama, “remedy”), related to ἰάομαι (iáomai, “to heal”) + -logy.

parole.significato: An ancient people who dwelt north of and inland from the Liburnians, off the Adriatic coast and eastwards of the Istria…
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek Ἰάποδες (Iápodes).

parole.significato: Of or pertaining to a physician or physicians.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἰατρικός (iatrikós, “medical”).

parole.significato: Medical treatment; doctor; physician.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ῑ̓ᾱτρο- (īātro-), combining form of ἰατρός (iatrós, “doctor”).

parole.significato: The culture of medical professionals.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἰατρός (iatrós, “physician”); iatro- + culture.

parole.significato: imitative or figurative expression
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek εἴκασμα (eíkasma, “likeness”), from εἰκάζω (eikázō).

parole.significato: Denoting a trace or trace amounts.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἴχνος (íkhnos, “footprint”).

parole.significato: A radioactive thorium molybdate mineral found in Sardinia.
parole.testo: From Latin Ichnūsa (“Sardinia”, from Ancient Greek Ἰχνοῦσα (Ikhnoûsa)) + -ite.

parole.significato: Of, pertaining to, or like fish; piscine.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἰχθυϊκός (ikhthuïkós). By surface analysis, ichthy- + -ic.

parole.significato: fish
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ῐ̓χθῡ́ς (ĭkhthū́s, “fish”).

parole.significato: Relating to, or causing, ichthyoallyeinotoxism.
parole.testo: From the stems of Ancient Greek ἰχθύς (ikhthús, “fish”), ἀλλοιόω (alloióō, “to become mad”) and τοξικόν (toxikón, “poison”).

parole.significato: A centaurian sea being with the upper body of a human, the lower anterior half and forelegs of a horse, and the tailed…
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἰχθυοκένταυρος (ikhthuokéntauros).

parole.significato: One of the spiny plates found on the back and tail of certain skates.
parole.testo: From ichthyo- + Ancient Greek δόρυ (dóru) + -lite.

parole.significato: The ammonium salt of sulfonated bitumen; used to treat some forms of skin diseases
parole.testo: Ancient Greek ἰχθύς (ikhthús, “fish”) + -ol, since it is an oily mixture prepared by dry distillation of a bituminous mineral containing fossil fishes.

parole.significato: That which consumes fish; any fish-eating thing or (more rarely) person.
parole.testo: From the Ancient Greek ἰχθυοφάγος (ikhthuophágos, “fish-eating”), and substantivised as a plurale tantum proper noun: “the Fish-eaters, the Ichthyophagi”; reinforced in the general sense (“that which consumes fish”) by the English ichthyo- (“fish”) + -phage (“eater”).

parole.significato: A form of apophyllite
parole.testo: Ancient Greek [Term?]

parole.significato: A parasitic infection of freshwater fish caused by the ciliate Ichthyophthirius multifiliis.
parole.testo: From Ichthyophthirius + -iasis, from Ancient Greek ἰχθύς (ikhthús, “fish”) + Ancient Greek φθείρ (phtheír, “louse”) + -ius.

parole.significato: A stylized representation of a fish, used as a Christian symbol.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ΙΧΘΥΣ (IKHTHUS, “fish”), which also served (repurposed) as an acronym (ΙΧΘΥΣ (IKHTHUS)) for Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, Θεοῦ Υἱός, Σωτήρ (Iēsoûs Khristós, Theoû Huiós, Sōtḗr, “Jesus Christ, Son of God, Savior”).

parole.significato: Forms terms relating to images or to icons
parole.testo: Equivalent to icon + -o-. From Ancient Greek εἰκών (eikṓn), as in terms such as εἰκονοκλάστης (eikonoklástēs).

parole.significato: A person who supports the veneration of religious icons; an iconophile or iconodulist
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ancient Greek εἰκονόδουλος (eikonódoulos), a compound of εἰκών (eikṓn, “likeness, image, portrait”) + δοῦλος (doûlos, “slave”).

parole.significato: The study of icons in art or art history.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek εἰκών (eikṓn, “icon”) + -logy.

parole.significato: Hostility to images as objects of worship.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek εἰκονομαχία (eikonomakhía), from εἰκών (eikṓn, "likeness, image, portrait") and -μαχία (-makhía, "battle, fight"), literally meaning "war against images" or "war on icons".

parole.significato: The use of pictographs to represent their sounds, as in English rebuses using an eye to mean I or in Chinese phonetic t…
parole.testo: A clipping of earlier icononomatic, from a modern combination of Ancient Greek εἰκών (eikṓn, “icon, image, likeness”) + ὄνομα (ónoma, “name”) + -ικός (-ikós, “-ic: forming adjectives”).

parole.significato: An illustration of a biological specimen that serves as a holotype or lectotype (type specimen and it becomes the type…
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek εἰκών (eikṓn, “figure, icon”) + τύπος (túpos, “blow, impression”).

parole.significato: twenty
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ancient Greek εἴκοσι (eíkosi, “twenty”).

parole.significato: A polygon with twenty sides and twenty angles.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek εἰκοσάγωνος (eikoságōnos, “having twenty sides”), from εἴκοσι (eíkosi, “twenty”) + γωνία (gōnía, “angle”). Equivalent to icosa- + -gon.

parole.significato: A polyhedron with twenty faces.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek εἰκοσάεδρον (eikosáedron), from εἴκοσι (eíkosi, “twenty”) + ἕδρα (hédra, “face of a geometrical solid”). Equivalent to icosa- + -hedron.

parole.significato: A polygon with twenty-one edges and twenty-one angles.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek εἰκοσιέν (eikosién, “twenty-one”) + -gon, from εἴκοσι (eíkosi) (twenty) + ἕν (hén) (one).

parole.significato: A four-dimensional object with no regular three-dimensional analogue, constructed out of twenty-four octahedra.
parole.testo: From icosi- (“twenty”) + tetra- (“four”) + -choron (“room”), from Ancient Greek εἴκοσι (eíkosi, “twenty”) τέτταρες (téttares, “four”) and χῶρος (khôros, “room”).

parole.significato: A neurological or cognitive phenomenon in which activation of a particular concept triggers a sensory-like experience.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἰδέα (idéa, “notion, pattern”) + -aesthesia, modeled after synaesthesia, and introduced by Danko Nikolić in.

parole.significato: Idea, image.
parole.testo: Representing a combining form of Ancient Greek ἰδέα (idéa, “form, semblance”). Unrelated to idio-.

parole.significato: individuality, peculiarity, separateness.
parole.testo: Representing a combining form of Ancient Greek ἴδιος (ídios, “own, personal, distinct”). By surface analysis, idi- + -o-. Unrelated to ideo-.

parole.significato: Pertaining or conforming to idiom, the natural mode of expression of a language.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἰδιωματικός (idiōmatikós, “related to an idiom”), from ἰδίωμα (idíōma, “idiom”).

parole.significato: A type of sticheron found in the liturgical books used in Orthodox Christianity.
parole.testo: Ancient Greek ἰδιόμελον (idiómelon)

parole.significato: The posterior portion of the body of a mite.
parole.testo: From idio- (“distinct”) + soma (“body”), from Ancient Greek σῶμα (sôma, “body”).

parole.significato: A behavior or way of thinking that is characteristic of a person or a group.
parole.testo: First attested in 1604, in modern sense since 1665, from Ancient Greek ἰδιοσυγκρασία (idiosunkrasía, “one’s own temperament”), from ἴδιος (ídios, “one’s own”) + σύν (sún, “together”) + κρᾶσις (krâsis, “temperament”). By surface analysis, idio- + syn- + -crasy.

parole.significato: Troy, an ancient city located in present-day Hisarlik, Turkey.
parole.testo: Ultimately from Ancient Greek Ἴλιον (Ílion).

parole.significato: A form of play that creates a temporary disruption of perception, for example by inducing vertigo, dizziness, disorient…
parole.testo: Via French from Ancient Greek ἶλιγξ (îlinx, “whirlpool; dizziness”), coined by French sociologist Roger Caillois in 1958.

parole.significato: a creature without feet
parole.testo: Coined on Latinate roots (im- + -ped) by Richard Owen in 1861 as a calque of Aristotle’s Ancient Greek ἀπούς (apoús).

parole.significato: A cephalic disorder characterized by spina bifida and spinal retroflexion
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἰνίον (iníon) + ἐγκέφαλος (enképhalos) + -y.

parole.significato: A small protuberance on the external surface of the back of the skull near the neck; the external occipital protuberanc…
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἰνίον (iníon, “occipital bone; back of the head”). Compare -ion (“anthropometric landmark”).

parole.significato: A complex nitrogenous substance formerly hypothesized to be continually decomposed and reproduced in the muscles during…
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἴς (ís, “power, muscle”) + -gen.

parole.significato: any silicate having interlocking chains of silicate tetrahedra
parole.testo: From ino- + silicate, from Ancient Greek ἴς, ἰνός (ís, inós, “fibre”).

parole.significato: Increasing or decreasing the force of muscular contractions.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἴς (ís, “sinew, tendon; strength, force”) + -tropic (“affecting, changing”), from Ancient Greek τρόπος (trópos, “turn, direction, way”) + -ικός (-ikós, “-ic”, adjectival suffix).

parole.significato: Of or pertaining to a segment sometimes present at the proximal end of the hyoid arch.
parole.testo: From inter- + -hyal, from Ancient Greek ὖ (û, “the letter upsilon”).

parole.significato: Containing iodine.
parole.testo: Derived from Ancient Greek ἰοειδής (ioeidḗs, “violet”).

parole.significato: The clear variety of cordierite, sometimes used as a gem.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἴον (íon, “violet”) + -lite.

parole.significato: An atom or group of atoms bearing an electrical charge, such as the sodium and chlorine atoms in a salt solution.
parole.testo: From the ending of anion and cation, which in turn is from Ancient Greek ἰόν (ión, “going”), neuter present participle of εἶμι (eîmi, “I go”). Coined by English polymath William Whewell in 1834 for Michael Faraday, who introduced it later that year.

parole.significato: Synonym of Ionian; of or relating to Ionia or the Ionians
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἰωνικός (iōnikós, “related to Ionians”).

parole.significato: Synonym of rubedo (“reddening process in the alchemical magnum opus”).
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἴωσις (íōsis), from ἰός (iós, “rust”).

parole.significato: The ninth letter of the Greek alphabet (Ι, ι).
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἰῶτα (iôta), ultimately from Proto-Semitic *yad- (“hand”). Doublet of jot and yodh. Sense “jot, small quantity” in reference to a phrase in the New Testament: ”one iote or one title, shall in no wise passe from the law”, iota being the smallest letter of the Greek alphabet.

parole.significato: Pronunciation of another vowel or diphthong as [i], or a vowel shift resulting in such pronunciation, especially in Gre…
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἰωτακισμός (iōtakismós), by surface analysis from iota + -cism (phenomenon related to a specific phoneme).

parole.significato: A specific occurrence of palatalization that occurred in the Proto-Slavic language, in which a consonant combined with…
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἰῶτα (iôta) + English -tion.

parole.significato: To precede a spoken vowel sound with a "y" sound, as the u in "pure" and "cute".
parole.testo: 1854 pre-iotized, 1874 iotization, iotized, 1890 iotised, 1906 iotise. Adapted from Ancient Greek ἰωτίζω (iōtízō, “I write with an iota”). Compare iota.

parole.significato: Promoting or fitted to promote peace or peacemaking, especially over disputes; conciliatory, non-confrontational, peace…
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek εἰρηνικός (eirēnikós, “characterized by peace, peaceful”) + English -ic (suffix forming adjectives with the sense ‘of or pertaining to’). Εἰρηνικός (Eirēnikós) is derived from εἰρήνη (eirḗnē, “peace”) (possibly from εἴρω (eírō, “to fasten together”) (ultimately from Proto-Indo-Eur

parole.significato: The study of peace.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek εἰρήνη (eirḗnē, “peace”) + -logy.

parole.significato: Relating to the iris.
parole.testo: From stem of Ancient Greek of ἶρις (îris, “the rainbow; colored circle, colored portion of the eye, something bent or curved”).

parole.significato: A surgical procedure for glaucoma in which a portion of the iris is incised and incarcerated in a limbal incision.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ῑ̓́ρῐδος (ī́rĭdos), genitive of Ancient Greek ἶρις (îris) + Ancient Greek ἔγκλεισις (énkleisis). By surface analysis, irid- + en- + -cleisis.

parole.significato: Total or partial absence of the iris of the eye.
parole.testo: From irid- + Ancient Greek ἐρῆμος (erêmos, “lonely”) + -ia.

parole.significato: (uncountable) A chemical element with an atomic number of 77: a very hard, brittle, silvery-white transition metal of t…
parole.testo: From international scientific vocabulary, from New Latin iridium, from Classical Latin iris + -ium, from Ancient Greek ἶρις (îris, “rainbow”), because of the bright colour of many of the element's salts.

parole.significato: A large group of early Germanic tribes who settled in the Elbe watershed and by the 1st century AD had expanded into Ba…
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek Ἑρμίονες (Hermíones).

parole.significato: A liturgical book containing irmoi for the various canons chanted during the morning service.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek εἱρμολόγιον (heirmológion).

parole.significato: The initial troparion of an ode of a canon.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ancient Greek εἱρμός (heirmós).

parole.significato: A state of doubt regarding one's own "vocabulary" (set of communicative beliefs) that cannot be removed by making argum…
parole.testo: Coined by American philosopher Richard Rorty, from Ancient Greek εἴρων (eírōn, “one who says less than they think”). By surface analysis, irony + -ism.

parole.significato: An equal of the Apostles.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἰσαπόστολος (isapóstolos).

parole.significato: A traitor.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek Ἰσκαριώτης (Iskariṓtēs)/ Ἰσκαριώθ (Iskariṓth); the original Hebrew or Aramaic term is unknown and the subject of much debate. For more information, see the name and background section of Wikipedia's article on Judas Iscariot.

parole.significato: Anhidrosis, the suppression or retention of sweating.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἴσχειν (ískhein, “hold back”) + hidrosis (“excessive sweat”).

parole.significato: ischium
parole.testo: Combining form of Ancient Greek ἰσχίον (iskhíon, “ischium”).

parole.significato: One of a pair of conjoined twins who are united at the pelvis.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἴσχιον (ískhion, “hip”) + πάγος (págos, “fixed, set”) (from πήγνυμι (pḗgnumi, “fasten, fix, set”)); equivalent to ischio- + -pagus.

parole.significato: equality of all citizens in freedom of speech, specially in public assemblies.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἰσηγορία (isēgoría).

parole.significato: Hatred of Islam or Muslims.
parole.testo: From Islamo- + -misia, from Ancient Greek μῑσέω (mīséō, “to hate”) or μῖσος (mîsos, “hatred”), coined as an alternative to Islamophobia.

parole.significato: Same, identical.
parole.testo: Internationalism. Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἴσος (ísos, “equal”).

parole.significato: A line drawn on a map or chart connecting places of equal or constant pressure.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἴσος (ísos, “equal”) + βάρος (báros, “weight”), equivalent to iso- + bar-.

parole.significato: A line on a map or chart joining places of equal depth of water; a depth contour.
parole.testo: From iso- + Ancient Greek βαθύς (bathús, “deep”) (see bathy-).

parole.significato: An isoline drawn through geographical points at which a given phase of thunderstorm activity occurred simultaneously.
parole.testo: From iso- + Ancient Greek βροντή (brontḗ, “thunder”) (see bronto-).

parole.significato: A peculiarity in the design of bas-relief, and also in painting, in which the heads of human figures are depicted at th…
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek, meaning "like-headed". See iso- + cephalon.

parole.significato: A line connecting places on the Earth's surface that have the same mean frequency of auroras.
parole.testo: From iso- + Ancient Greek χάσμα (khásma, “abyss, chasm”). See chasma.

parole.significato: An isotherm connecting points on a map with equal mean winter temperature.
parole.testo: From iso- + Ancient Greek χεῖμα (kheîma, “cold, winter”).

parole.significato: In general, a place or position with relevant parameters matching other places, as in having the same pressure, chemist…
parole.testo: From iso- + Ancient Greek χώρα (khṓra, “place”).

parole.significato: Having the same duration.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἴσος (ísos, “equal”) + χρόνος (khrónos, “time”) + -al.

parole.significato: Happening at regular intervals; isochronal.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἴσος (ísos, “equal”) + Ancient Greek χρόνος (khrónos, “time”) + -ous.

parole.significato: The state of being isochronous.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἴσος (ísos, “equal”) + χρόνος (khrónos, “time”) + -y.

parole.significato: Of uniform color; isochromatic.
parole.testo: From iso- + Ancient Greek χρώς (khrṓs, “color”) + -ous.

parole.significato: A rhetorical scheme in which parallel elements possess the same number of words or syllables.
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἰσόκωλον (isókōlon), neuter of ἰσόκωλος (isókōlos), from ἴσος (ísos, “equal”) and κῶλον (kôlon, “member, clause”). By surface analysis, iso- + colon.

parole.significato: The condition of having the pupils of both eyes the same size
parole.testo: From iso- + Ancient Greek κόρη (kórē, “pupil”).

parole.significato: Of or relating to isocracy.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἰσοκρατία (isokratía, “equality of strength or power”) + -ic.

parole.significato: An isoline connecting points on the Earth's surface having the same mean temperature in the coldest month of the year.
parole.testo: From iso- + Ancient Greek κρυμός (krumós, “cold, chilliness”) (see κρύος (krúos)). Coined by James D. Dana in 1854, who glossed κρυμός as "extreme cold".

parole.significato: A form of masonry in which the vertical joint of each course is in the middle of the block beneath.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ancient Greek ἰσόδομον (isódomon), from ἴσο- (íso-) + a noun derived from δέμω (démō, “to build”).

parole.significato: A line of equal or constant dew point on a graph or chart, such as a weather map.
parole.testo: From iso- + Ancient Greek δρόσος (drósos, “dew”) + Ancient Greek θερμός (thermós, “warm”) (equivalent to thermo-).

parole.significato: An isoline connecting places at which an equal amount of wind power is available near ground level on average.
parole.testo: From iso- + Ancient Greek δύναμις (dúnamis, “power”). Coined by Jack W. Reed in 1975.

parole.significato: A line on a map indicating the geographical boundaries of a linguistic feature.
parole.testo: From iso- + gloss, ultimately from Ancient Greek ἴσος (ísos, “equal”) (possibly from Proto-Indo-European *wi- (“to separate”)) + γλῶσσα (glôssa, “tongue; language”) (ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *glōgʰs).

parole.significato: Equality of freedom of speech and expression; the right of each citizen of a city (or other unit) to speak in public, t…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ancient Greek ἰσηγορία (isēgoría).

parole.significato: An isohaline.
parole.testo: From iso- + Ancient Greek ἅλς (háls, “salt”) + -ine.

parole.significato: A line on a map connecting places that receive equal solar radiation, or equal daily hours of sunshine.
parole.testo: From iso- + Ancient Greek ἥλιος (hḗlios, “sun”).

parole.significato: A line of equal rainfall on a map or chart, such as a weather map.
parole.testo: From iso- + Ancient Greek ὑετός (huetós, “rain”).

parole.significato: A contour line; a line on a map connecting points of equal height.
parole.testo: From iso- + Ancient Greek ὕψος (húpsos, “height”) (see hypso-).

parole.significato: Having flagella of equal length.
parole.testo: From iso- (“equal”) + -kont (“flagellate”) from Ancient Greek κοντός (kontós, “pole”).

parole.significato: An isoline indicating equal cloud cover.
parole.testo: From iso- + Ancient Greek νέφος (néphos, “cloud”) (see nepho-).

parole.significato: Equality before the law; possession of equal rights; equal distribution of rights and privileges.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ancient Greek ἰσονομία (isonomía). By surface analysis, iso- + -nomia.

parole.significato: The same, or equal, in law or right; one in kind or origin; analogous or similar.
parole.testo: From iso- + Ancient Greek νόμος (nómos, “law”) + -ic.

parole.significato: A line on a chart joining parts of a stratigraphic unit that have the same thickness; an isopachous line.
parole.testo: From iso- + Ancient Greek παχύς (pakhús, “thick”) (see pachy-).

parole.significato: Having leaves of equal size and shape throughout.
parole.testo: Ancient Greek, from iso- + -phyllous.

parole.significato: Having equal pressure; isobaric.
parole.testo: From iso- + an element derived from Ancient Greek πίεσις (píesis, “pressure”) (see πιέζω (piézō)).

parole.significato: A line drawn on a map through all points having the same value of some measurable quantity.
parole.testo: From iso- + Ancient Greek πλῆθος (plêthos, “a great number”).

parole.significato: Equal rights of citizenship in different communities; mutual political rights.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἰσοπολιτεία (isopoliteía), from ἰσοπολίτης (isopolítēs, “citizen with equal rights”), from ἴσος (ísos, “equal, same”) + πολίτης (polítēs, “citizen”).

parole.significato: A line on a map that joins places of equal annual change in a geomagnetic property; an isoporic line.
parole.testo: From iso- + Ancient Greek πόρος (póros, “journey”), on the basis that isopors are "lines of equal travel".

parole.significato: An isoline.
parole.testo: From iso- + Ancient Greek πρακτικός (praktikós, “fit for action, effective”) (see practise).

parole.significato: Of points on a surface, or in a medium: having equal density.
parole.testo: From from Ancient Greek ἴσος (ísos, “equal”) + Ancient Greek πυκνός (puknós, “thick”).

parole.significato: Having a constant or equal absorption
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek iso- + σβεστός (sbestós, “extinguished”), verbal adjective to σβέννυμι (sbénnumi, “I extinguish”).

parole.significato: The state of balance or pressure equilibrium thought to exist within the Earth's crust, whereby the upper lithosphere f…
parole.testo: From iso- + Ancient Greek στάσις (stásis, “a standing”).

parole.significato: Having the same number of stamens as petals.
parole.testo: From iso- + Ancient Greek στήμων (stḗmōn).

parole.significato: The state of arguments having equal strength or persuasiveness; equipollent.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ancient Greek ἰσοσθένεια (isosthéneia, “equal strength”)

parole.significato: The excretion of urine whose specific gravity (concentration) is neither greater nor less than that of protein-free pla…
parole.testo: From iso-, Ancient Greek σθένος (sthénos), + -uria.

parole.significato: An isoline linking places on a map which have equal wind speed.
parole.testo: From iso- + Ancient Greek ταχύς (takhús, “fast”) (see tachy-).

parole.significato: A line drawn through points of equal temperature in a vertical section of the ocean.
